judge_response:
ANALYSIS: “Hirschsprung’s disease” and “Hirschsprung disease” are orthographic variants — the former uses the possessive apostrophe (historically common), while the latter omits it (increasingly preferred in modern medical nomenclature, e.g., per WHO ICD-11, UMLS, and major textbooks like Nelson’s Pediatrics and Robbins & Cotran). Both refer unambiguously to the same congenital disorder characterized by absence of ganglion cells in the myenteric and submucosal plexuses of the distal colon. No clinical, diagnostic, or semantic distinction exists between the two forms.

VERDICT: CORRECT
